about: E5 gold set: claims a draft makes about papers in the library, written by reading those papers. 'supported' claims restate a statement of the cited paper; 'unsupported' ones change its method, a number, or reverse its finding. 'evidence' is a short phrase that the passage stating the fact contains, used to measure retrieval separately from the verdicts. Items 'e5-m*' are one sentence citing two papers, judged once per paper.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
items.claim: RAG comes in two variants: RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document for the whole output, while RAG-Token can use a different document for each token.
items.sentence: RAG comes in two variants: RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document for the whole output, while RAG-Token can use a different document for each token (Lewis et al., 2020).

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
items.claim: RAG generates the whole answer from the single top-ranked document, without marginalizing over the retrieved documents.
items.sentence: RAG generates the whole answer from the single top-ranked document, without marginalizing over the retrieved documents (Lewis et al., 2020).

items.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

items.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

items.claim: DPR encodes questions and passages with two independent BERT networks.

items.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
items.claim: In Fusion-in-Decoder, each retrieved passage is processed independently by the encoder and the passages are combined jointly in the decoder.

items.claim: Fusion-in-Decoder keeps improving as the number of retrieved passages grows, up to one hundred passages.

items.claim: REALM pre-trains a knowledge retriever without supervision, using masked language modeling as the learning signal and backpropagating through the retrieval step.

items.claim: RECITE first recites relevant passages from the model's own memory by sampling and then produces the answer, instead of retrieving documents.

items.claim: Self-RAG trains a single language model to retrieve on demand and to reflect on its own generations with special reflection tokens.
